heading.en: Why can no engine turn all its heat into work?
heading.kn: ಯಾವ ಎಂಜಿನ್ ಕೂಡ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಉಷ್ಣವನ್ನು ಕೆಲಸವಾಗಿ ಏಕೆ ಬದಲಿಸಲಾರದು?

hook.en: Energy is conserved, so why not run a ship by taking heat out of the sea? The first law allows it. A *second* law forbids it.
hook.kn: ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಿತ, ಹಾಗಾದರೆ ಸಮುದ್ರದಿಂದ ಉಷ್ಣ ತೆಗೆದು ಹಡಗು ಓಡಿಸಬಾರದೇಕೆ? ಮೊದಲ ನಿಯಮ ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಅವಕಾಶ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡನೇ ನಿಯಮ ತಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: State the Kelvin–Planck and Clausius statements
Find the efficiency of a heat engine

say.en: Energy is conserved, so why not run a ship by taking heat out of the sea? The first law allows it. A second law forbids it. In this lesson: State the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements.
Find the efficiency of a heat engine.
Tell reversible from irreversible processes.

body.en: Kelvin–Planck statement: no process is possible whose sole result is the absorption of heat from a reservoir and its complete conversion into work. Clausius statement: no process is possible whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a colder body to a hotter body. So a heat engine taking Q₁ from a hot source must reject some heat Q₂ to a cold sink; its efficiency η = W/Q₁ = 1 − Q₂/Q₁ is always less than 1.
body.kn: ಕೆಲ್ವಿನ್–ಪ್ಲ್ಯಾಂಕ್: ಉಷ್ಣವನ್ನು ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣವಾಗಿ ಕೆಲಸವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುವುದೇ ಏಕೈಕ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶವಾಗಿರುವ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಕ್ಲಾಸಿಯಸ್: ತಂಪು ವಸ್ತುವಿನಿಂದ ಬಿಸಿ ವಸ್ತುವಿಗೆ ಉಷ್ಣ ತಾನಾಗಿ ಹರಿಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಎಂಜಿನ್ ದಕ್ಷತೆ η = 1 − Q₂/Q₁ < 1.

say.en: Kelvin-Planck statement: no process is possible whose sole result is the absorption of heat from a reservoir and its complete conversion into work. Clausius statement: no process is possible whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a colder body to a hotter body. So a heat engine taking Q 1 from a hot source must reject some heat Q 2 to a cold sink; its efficiency eta equals W over Q 1 equals 1 - Q 2 over Q 1 is always less than 1. say.en: Clausius: no self-acting refrigerator.
eta equals W over Q 1 equals 1 - Q 2 over Q 1.

title.en: Heat engines and the second law

say.en: Every heat engine takes heat Q1 from a hot source, turns part of it into work W, and rejects Q2 to a cold sink.
Energy is conserved, so W is Q1 minus Q2. Efficiency is the work out divided by the heat in.
An engine takes 1000 joule and rejects 600 joule: it does 400 joule of work, an efficiency of 40 percent.
Kelvin–Planck: Q2 can never be zero. No engine turns heat completely into work. Clausius: heat does not flow by itself from cold to hot.
A reversible process can be run backwards, returning system and surroundings to their start. Real processes are irreversible.

explanation.en: A process is reversible only if it is quasi-static (always in equilibrium) and has no dissipation: no friction, no free expansion, no heat flow across a finite temperature difference, no mixing. Real processes are irreversible; reversible ones are ideal limits, like the strokes of a Carnot engine.
explanation.kn: ಅರೆ-ಸ್ಥಿರ (ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಸಮತೋಲನ) ಮತ್ತು ಶಕ್ತಿ ವ್ಯಯವಿಲ್ಲದ (ಘರ್ಷಣೆ, ಮುಕ್ತ ವಿಸ್ತರಣೆ, ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ತಾಪ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸದ ಉಷ್ಣ ಹರಿವು, ಮಿಶ್ರಣ ಇಲ್ಲದ) ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಉತ್ಕ್ರಮಣೀಯ. ನಿಜ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳು ಅನುತ್ಕ್ರಮಣೀಯ; ಉತ್ಕ್ರಮಣೀಯವು ಕಾರ್ನೋ ಎಂಜಿನ್ ಹಂತಗಳಂತೆ ಆದರ್ಶ ಮಿತಿಗಳು.

body.en: A process is *reversible* if it can be turned back so that both the system and the surroundings return to their original states with no other change. This needs a quasi-static process with no dissipative effects such as friction or viscosity. Real processes are irreversible: free expansion of a gas, heat flowing across a finite temperature difference, and friction are examples.
body.kn: ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸುತ್ತಮುತ್ತಲು ಎರಡೂ ಮೂಲ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗೆ ಮರಳಬಹುದಾದರೆ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿಸಬಹುದಾದದ್ದು. ಅದು ಅರೆಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗಿದ್ದು ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಇರಬಾರದು. ಮುಕ್ತ ವ್ಯಾಕೋಚನ, ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿಸಲಾಗದವು.

problem.en: An engine takes 1000 J of heat from a hot source in each cycle and rejects 600 J to the sink. Find the work done per cycle and the efficiency.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An engine takes 1000 J of heat from a hot source in each cycle and rejects 600 J to the sink. Find the work done per cycle and the efficiency.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An engine takes 1000 joules of heat from a hot source in each cycle and rejects 600 joules to the sink. Find the work done per cycle and the efficiency.
W equals Q 1 - Q 2 equals 1000 minus 600 equals 400 joules.
eta equals W over Q 1 equals 400 over 1000 equals 0.4.
So the answer is 400 joules; 40 percent.
